newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end firmer, platinum surges.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end firmer, platinum surges.

text.p: New York precious metals ended firmer Tuesday as markets reopened after the Memorial Day holiday, with a surge in platinum and palladium helping to boost the complex and gold shrugging off latest Bundesbank revaluation announcements, dealers said.

Increasing talk by European central banks about reserves revalution was opening the door to a more active management of reserves and discussion about price risk, said Dinsa Mehta, managing director of global commodities at Chase Manhattan.
"But the market seems to be taking this in its stride," Mehta said.
Germany's Bundesbank was expected on Wednesday to approve a revalution of its gold reserves which could swell Germany's federal coffers by up to 12 billion markets, government sources said Tuesday.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said Tuesday a special interim Bundesbank balance sheet had been drawn up and Bonn could benefit from the revaluation payout later this year.
Dutch Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said Tuesday the next revalution of the country's gold reserves at the end of 1998 will at least quintuple their value.
COMEX June gold settled $1.60 higher at $344.70 an ounce, traded $345.30 to $344.00.
Volume was estimated at 51,000 lots, but much of this was due to rollover from the June contract to August, ahead of the first delivery day on Friday, dealers said.
"We are seeing at least signs that the speculative market is short," Mehta said of the rollover.
COMEX silver was listless and narrowly traded, failing to glean any significant upside momentum from the gains in gold and white metals.
COMEX July silver settled 1.0 cent firmer at $4.748 an ounce, traded $4.76 to $4.73.

White metals had begun strengthening overnight in Tokyo on shortcovering as short positions held by private investors in TOCOM palladium futures rose to about 59 tonnes after fresh short positions were added, local dealers said.
Nervousness hit platinum Tuesday following reports of an illegal strike at Rustenburg Platinum Mines in an already tight market, analyst Jim Steel of Refco said.

The surge in platinum and palladium, the former moving above $400 an ounce to a three-month high in the July contract, was also linked to a big increase in lease rates, or the borrowing cost, for palladium Tuesday, dealers said.
Palladium's one month lease rate raced up to 40 percent Tuesday from 25 percent last week. High lease rates are usually a sign of a tight physical market.
Dealers said there may be skepticism over Russia's plan to begin shipping 1997 platinum and palladium exports soon.
September NYMEX palladium, now most active, ended $2.30 firmer at $170.00 an ounce, with spot June going out $3.80 higher at $174.50 an ounce.
July NYMEX platinum settled $8.60 higher at $397.00 an ounce, traded $401.00 to $392.50.
